# Disagreement Log — T12_006 (Testament of Zebulun)
**Chapter:** T12_006 | **Verses:** 7 sections (~10 verses)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 2:3–4 | Zebulun's emotional reaction | "my-liver-was-poured-out, and-all-the-substance-of-my-bowels-was-loosened" | Same (formal) | "My whole body shook" | EMET/LOGOS literal retained — this is the Hebrew idiom for visceral emotional response; PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the bodily specificity |
| 2 | 3:2 | Why brothers accused Joseph | EMET: "He came to Dothan to spy on our doings" | LOGOS: "He spied on us, and came to Dothan to see our doings" | Omits accusation detail | Both EMET/LOGOS accusation retained; PNEUMA omission rejected |
| 3 | 3:3 | Price paid | "twenty-pieces-of-gold" (EMET) | "twenty pieces of gold" | "twenty pieces of silver" | "twenty pieces of gold" — Greek chrysōn; the Genesis MT has silver but the Greek MS here has gold; PNEUMA error |
| 4 | 5:2–3 | Compassion/wealth paradox | Formal, compressed | Full expansion with two-part contrast | "rich before God / poor before God" | SOPHIA adopts the two-part antithesis — richest theological statement of the chapter |
| 5 | 6:4–5 | Verse 6:5 duplication | EMET has 6:5 as distinct | LOGOS also includes | PNEUMA omits | SOPHIA retains as emphasis — the "dwelling place" formula concludes both the exhortation and the chapter |

---
*SOPHIA notes: Testament of Zebulun is the compassion chapter par excellence. The key phrase "bowels of mercy" (splanchna eleous) is the source of the New Testament's splanchnizomai — "moved with compassion." All three translators handle the Joseph weeping scene well. The price discrepancy (gold vs. silver) is a known MS variant; SOPHIA follows the Codex Cantabrigiensis Greek.*
